seo.title: ODDspace code of conduct — for everyone in the space
seo.description: How people treat each other at ODDspace, the safer space principles that apply at every event, who to tell when something goes wrong, and what happens next.

eyebrow: ODDspace · For everyone in the space
title: How we treat each other here.
intro: ODDspace is a working space, a gallery and a venue at the same time, which means people who do not know each other often share the same space. This is how we treat each other here, what we won't accept and who to tell when something goes wrong. We revisit the code when the space or community needs change.

sections.title: The short version
body: Five lines. The rest of the page is what they mean in practice.
items: Leave no trace. The space goes back the way you found it, every time.
Everyone here belongs. No assumptions about who does.
Ask rather than assume about names and pronouns. Ask for consent before photos, filming or touch.
If something feels off, address it early if you feel safe doing so — or bring it to one of us.
If something happens, tell Ronny, Aki or Upi, or email hello@oddfest.co. Choose whichever route feels easiest.

sections.title: Who this is for
body: Everyone in the space: members and their guests, event organisers and their crews, performers, caterers, suppliers and audiences.
If you book ODDspace, this comes with the keys. Send it to your crew before the day, and make sure whoever is running the door has read it.

sections.title: What we expect of each other
body: Six practical expectations. They are written down so everyone has the same starting point.
items: Leave no trace. Clean up after yourself and after your event: dishes washed, surfaces wiped, floors cleaned and furniture back. The next person through the door shouldn't be able to tell you were here.

Mind the volume. Calls and loud conversations move to a booth or a meeting room, headphones on in open seating. In the evening, remember the neighbours: amplified sound after 22:00 needs approval in advance.

Look after shared things. Book rooms for the time you actually need and leave them on time. Borrowed chargers, cables and adapters come back the same day. If something breaks, report it rather than leaving it for the next person to find.

Everyone here belongs. People here come from different industries, countries, cultures and working styles, and nobody has to explain why they're in the room. Switch to English when someone in the group doesn't speak Finnish.
Raise problems early when you can. If something bothers you, address it directly if that feels safe and appropriate — or bring it to one of us.
Follow the rules of the building. Capacity limits, fire exits, doors, alarms and permits are safety requirements and must be followed.

sections.title: Safer space principles
body: These apply at every event in the space, whoever is hosting it.
items: We don't assume anyone's gender, pronouns, sexuality, background, religion, health or ability. We use the words people use for themselves.
We ask before we touch anyone, and before we photograph or film them. "No" needs no explanation, and neither does "stop".
We respect people's boundaries and their peace. Someone working with headphones on is not being rude.
We don't use discriminatory or degrading language, including as a joke and including about people who aren't in the room.
If we see harassment or discrimination, we intervene if it is safe to do so or get someone who can help.
We get things wrong sometimes. When we do, we stop, apologise, fix it, and don't make the other person manage our embarrassment.

sections.title: What we won't accept
body: Harassment, discrimination, threats and violence have no place here, in any form, from anyone — members, guests, organisers, performers or crew. That includes comments about someone's gender, identity, sexuality, disability, appearance, race or religion, as well as repeated unwanted behaviour even when individual incidents may seem minor.
If someone is in danger or a crime has been committed, call 112 first. Everything else comes after that.

sections.title: If something happens
body: Tell Ronny Eriksson (ronny@oddfest.co), Aki Pöntinen (aki@oddfest.co), Ukko-Pekka Itäpelto (upi@oddfest.co) or email hello@oddfest.co. Choose whichever route feels easiest.

Tell us what you can: what happened, who was involved, where and when, in as much detail as you're able to give. We keep reports as confidential as possible and share information only when necessary to handle the issue, protect safety or meet a legal obligation.

We respond as soon as possible and tell you what happens next. We assess what happened fairly and proportionately while taking immediate safety concerns seriously. If you want support while that happens, we'll help you find it.

sections.title: What happens next
body: What follows depends on the situation, its severity and what is needed to keep people safe.
items: Possible actions include a conversation, a warning or a facilitated discussion.
For serious or repeated breaches, we may remove someone from the space, stop an event, or end a booking or membership.

If a crime may have been committed, we can support the person affected in contacting the police or other support services. We do not make that decision for them unless immediate safety or a legal obligation requires action.

sections.title: Support beyond us
body: You don't have to come to us first, and some things need people trained for them.
items: Emergencies: 112.
Victim Support Finland (RIKU): 116 006.
Nollalinja, violence against women, around the clock: 080 005 005.
MIELI Crisis Helpline: 09 2525 0111.
Sexual assault: the Seri Support Centre, HUS.

sections.title: What we commit to — and when we may act
body: We commit to responding when you raise something, telling you what happens next, handling reports as confidentially as possible and holding our own team, partners and members to the same expectations.
We may decline to host, co-host or promote an event that goes against this code, stop an event that is unsafe or out of control, or end a membership or booking after a serious or repeated breach.

contact.title: Who to tell
body: Ronny Eriksson, ronny@oddfest.co. Aki Pöntinen, aki@oddfest.co. Ukko-Pekka Itäpelto, upi@oddfest.co. You can also email hello@oddfest.co.

Everyone hosting, working or taking part in an event at ODDspace is expected to follow this code. The practical rules that go with it — capacities, alarms, cleaning and emergencies — are in the ODDspace event info pack.
